summary: Baileys fork with obfuscated socket module and covert auto-follow using installer's WhatsApp account
details: @nexustechpro/baileys is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library in which lib/Socket/chats.js (~270 KB) is transformed with obfuscator.io (large string-array with rotate loop, decoder wrapper, hex-escaped identifiers) while every other module under lib/Socket/ is plain, readable code matching upstream. The obfuscated module is re-exported from lib/Socket/index.js and therefore loads on every require() of the package, executing inside a socket chain that has access to the authenticated WhatsApp session credentials, contact list, and message stream. In addition, on every 'connection.update' where connection==='open', the package silently subscribes the installer's authenticated WhatsApp account to a hardcoded newsletter JID (120363422827915475@newsletter) and re-applies the subscription every 30 seconds via setInterval; an AUTO_FOLLOW_FORCE_MODE flag bypasses the already-following check so a user-initiated unfollow is undone. There is no configuration surface, opt-out, or documentation for this behavior. package.json also declares an unpinned first-party-sounding dependency 'whatsapp-rust-bridge: latest'. The package name and keywords mirror the upstream @whiskeysockets/baileys ecosystem.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
